questions.q: Why can't a single Master-Detail field, by itself, model a many-to-many relationship?
options: Master-Detail fields can't be created on custom objects
A Master-Detail field only ever points to one parent record, not many
Master-Detail fields are read-only
Salesforce disables Master-Detail on objects with more than one relationship
questions.explain: Each Master-Detail field connects its child to a single parent — modeling 'many on both sides' requires a separate object in between.

options: A report that joins two objects together
A field that stores a comma-separated list of record IDs
A custom object built with two Master-Detail relationships, one to each side being connected
A standard Salesforce object like Account or Contact
questions.explain: A junction object exists purely to connect two other objects, using two Master-Detail relationships — one to each parent.

questions.q: What does one row on a junction object represent?
options: A duplicate of the parent record
Every possible pairing between the two related objects
A summary of all related records
A single pairing between one record on each side
questions.explain: Each junction record represents exactly one pairing — add ten related records and you get ten junction records, not ten new fields.

questions.q: A Property is deleted. What happens to junction records (like Favorite or Offer) whose Master-Detail field points to that Property?
options: They are deleted too, because Master-Detail cascades on deletion
They are automatically reassigned to a different Property
Salesforce blocks the deletion until the junction records are manually removed
They are left in place with a blank Property field
questions.explain: A junction object's fields are real Master-Detail relationships, so deleting the parent cascades and deletes the junction records, same as any Master-Detail child.

questions.q: To an end user viewing a parent record, what does a many-to-many relationship built on a junction object look like?
options: A formula field showing a count
A separate tab that only admins can see
A warning banner explaining the junction object
An ordinary related list, just like any other relationship
questions.explain: The junction object is invisible plumbing from the user's perspective — it simply produces a normal-looking related list of connected records.
